newsitem.title: USA: Dow index soars 95 points to post biggest weekly gain.
newsitem.headline: Dow index soars 95 points to post biggest weekly gain.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average soared nearly 95 points Friday to post its biggest weekly gain ever on news of a plan to balance the U.S. federal budget.
The blue-chip rally was more than matched by the Nasdaq index, which posted its largest one-day point rise ever.
The Dow gained 94.72 points, or 1.36 percent, to close at 7,071.20. For the week, it was up a record 332.33 points, which beat the old record of 312 points set in the week ending April 18.
In the broader market, advancing issues swamped declines 2,120 to 477 on heavy volume of 499 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The market racked up huge gains this week on upbeat corporate earnings and good reports on the economy.
The Nasdaq Composite index jumped 34.83 in its biggest one-day gain to end at 1,305.33. The old high was set last July 17 when it rose 33.18 points.

The market got off to a solid start with the release of monthly jobs and wage data. The report showed a smaller-than-expected rise in payrolls and a drop in the average hourly wage, alleviating concerns about wage-driven inflation.
Clouding the issue for analysts, however, was a stunning decline in the nation's unemployment rate to 4.9 percent, the lowest level in 23 years.
"The market dodged a bullet with the jobs number," said Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist at Kemper Funds.
"But the reality is, if you want to look at something that's going to cause a pre-emptive rate increase, it's unemployment below 5 percent," he said.

The data, which reinforced the impression of an economy that is growing at a solid clip without sparking inflation, prompted a sharp advance in economically sensitive sectors like technology and transportation stocks.
The Dow Jones Transportation index jumped 61.65 points or 2.42 percent to an all-time high 2,605.83.

But investors held back from blue chips early in the session, checked by the surprise in the unemployment figures. That concern seemed to lifted when news of the balanced budget deal broke in late afternoon trading.
"For years, Fed Chairman Greenspan himself has said a balanced budget would lead to lower rates," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
"This market had been getting ready for a melt-up," he said, "and now here we are, knocking at the door of all-time highs."

The Dow's closing level put it just about 14 points shy of its record closing high of 7,085.16. In three weeks, the blue-chip index has exploded with a 10.6 percent rise and nearly wiped out its month-long correction.
The whirlwind finish to the week had some arguing that, once again, a significant pause is in order.
"I think we've overdone it here," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co.

With respect to the balanced budget deal in particular, he said, "We're seeing initially a reaction that's very clearly positive but the benefits are all in the out years, so the real impact remains to be seen."

Among individual issues, Novellus Systems Inc. jumped 6-7/8 to 69-3/8 on talk of a merger or a settlement of the patent suit between Novellus and semiconductor equipment rival Applied Materials Inc. Novellus did not respond to inquiries about the rumours.
Applied Materials, which declined comment on the rumours, gained 3-1/8 to 57-5/8.
Fisher Scientific International Inc. skidded 5-3/8 to 36-3/4. The scientific equipment supplier warned investors its near-term revenue growth would fall short of historic levels.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 14.44 points to 812.97. The American Stock Exchange index jumped 10.00 to 568.50.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 7.26 to 422.97. The average share was up 73 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,655.704 up 143.30 or 1.91 percent.
